title: Debugging and Troubleshooting Tools
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose of debugging and troubleshooting tools and explain at least one listed subtopic.
Interpret the example related to debugging and troubleshooting tools and predict its expected result.
Identify one validation, compatibility, security, or troubleshooting consideration relevant to the example.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore debugging and troubleshooting tools within XML Debugging, Testing, and Quality Assurance. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: Debugging and Troubleshooting Tools matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about xml validators, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Reliable XML engineering distinguishes syntax errors, schema violations, transformation defects, and application-level contract failures. Good tests use representative fixtures and assert both successful cases and controlled failures.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: XML validators; XPath evaluators; XSLT debugging; Structured diff tools; Logs and reproducible minimal examples. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Debugging and Troubleshooting Tools
content_blocks.code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

valid = "<catalog><product sku="P-101"/></catalog>"
root = ET.fromstring(valid)
assert root.tag == "catalog"
assert root.find("product").get("sku") == "P-101"
print("XML structure checks passed")
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. Keep valid, malformed, schema-invalid, namespace-rich, empty, and boundary fixtures. Assert useful error information without exposing secrets or leaking internal file/network paths.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the sample to its exact starting state before each experiment. Change one element, attribute, expression, or constraint at a time, then compare the result with the expected behavior.
content_blocks.limitations: This is a small test on trusted sample text. Production tests should also cover malformed inputs, schema violations, namespaces, large documents, resolver restrictions, and useful error reporting.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Distinguish well-formedness, schema validity, and application-level correctness; they are different checks.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small synthetic example that demonstrates “XML validators”. Then add one boundary case involving “XPath evaluators”. Write down what should happen before testing, and record the exact output or processor message afterward.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a document is correct because it looks readable.
common_mistakes.why: Visual appearance does not prove well-formedness, schema validity, correct namespace handling, or application-level meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse and validate the document with the intended processor, then assert its meaning using a focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing specification features with processor support.
common_mistakes.why: A standard may define features that a specific runtime does not implement.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the version and feature support; test with the actual target processor.

common_mistakes.why: Missing values, wrong types, namespace differences, or boundary inputs can expose failures.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a valid case, an invalid case, and an edge case to the verification notes.
